capabilities: Preserve long stack traces across callback and async boundaries
Toggle debug messages for any installed plugin from a view, commands, or settings
Open DevTools in the mobile app and manage debug library namespaces
Disable task timeouts while paused on a breakpoint and abort runaway operations
Diagnose out-of-memory crashes with heap readouts, on-disk samples, and heap snapshots
disambiguation: Not just a toggle for Obsidian's debug mode; it is a full toolkit of debugging aids for plugin development.
extras: Documentation is a demo vault included with each release and browsable on GitHub; async long stack traces and memory troubleshooting are desktop-only; beta versions install via BRAT.
intentEvidence: Obsidian's own debug mode, toggled from a command instead of the console
motivation: Debugging an Obsidian plugin meant guesswork because errors thrown inside callbacks or awaits lost their stack frames before reaching the console.
problem: Errors thrown inside callbacks or await chains arrive in the console with most of their stack trace missing, mobile Obsidian has no DevTools, and enabling per-plugin debug messages requires typing console commands.

relations.evidence: Alternative mobile DevTools through eruda; long stacks, debug namespaces, switches and task timeouts
Complementary console tooling; changes console output; no log file
Logstravaganza fork; external log files; UTC/local timestamps; plain text

summary: Debugging toolkit that preserves stack traces across async boundaries, toggles plugin debug messages from a UI, adds mobile DevTools, and helps diagnose memory crashes.
